### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via os migrate organization-ownership (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **36** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b81680e7800bee7f89bf58c3c0d4db10506a33eb` — the merge of head `319935d6ece1da93e202f8bc5d3184c927bfa757` into base `d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b81680e7800bee7f89bf58c3c0d4db10506a33eb && git checkout b81680e7800bee7f89bf58c3c0d4db10506a33eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2 319935d6ece1da93e202f8bc5d3184c927bfa757 && git checkout -B drift-repro d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2 && git merge --no-ff 319935d6ece1da93e202f8bc5d3184c927bfa757

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d79dc4883c5698cf05680a545758bdbba0d8a7a2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `319935d6ece1da93e202f8bc5d3184c927bfa757`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.declared-rule-mirrors.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.declared-rule-mirrors.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts, packages/cli/vitest.config.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts (`walkNullRows`, `TablePlan.unattributable`, `summary.unattributableRows`), packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts (`notNullExempt` rows `sys_sso_provider` and `sys_scim_provider`, `DECLARED_SHARING_RULE_SEEDER_RUNS`, `advisoryDepartureReason`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts (`translateDeclaredSharingRule`, `DeclaredSharingRuleSkip`; byte-identical to `origin/main`), packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts (`readMarker`, `assertOrganizationOwnershipMigrated`), packages/spec/src/system/migration.zod.ts (`isDataMigrationFlagVerified`), packages/platform-objects/src/system/migration-flag.ts (`recordDataMigrationRun`), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`buildDriverOptions`'s `tenantObject`), packages/cli/package.json with packages/cli/src/index.ts, console.ts and hook-body.ts (the `exports` map), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/package.json, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs (the `@objectstack/cli` registry entry), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired.ts (unchanged; the out-of-scope note). The two prose faces, `.changeset/15212-8c0-unattributable-rows-block.md` and `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, are judged in ①(f) and ②.

Rendered by an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of the adopting seat (`session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`), read-only: the net diff `origin/main...refs/review/pr-24403` (11 files, +474/−62, merge base `db4618b5`), the PR body and its one bot comment, card #15212's body and all 20 comments (plan 6251466182, amendments 6251607592 / 6252974640 / 6253205661 / 6254164222 / 6254733398, claim 6254514683, report 6255756719), decision #24352 and ruling 6251599171, ADR-0131 D10 / D13 / D14 on `origin/main`, PR #24376, and the head's check-runs. Head re-confirmed `319935d6e` at 2026-10-18T22:36Z.

**Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts):** 41 runs, 36 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, the dogfood matrix and verify, the packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance — each skipped by its own path filter), 0 failures. Read three times: at 22:25Z `Test Core` 2/6, 3/6 and 4/6 were `in_progress`; at 22:33Z only 3/6 was; at 22:36Z all six are `success`. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` leg, `Spec property liveness` and the three claim gates are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Ruling C, executed exactly — right.**
- Both populations the ruling names already live in one field. `organization-ownership-plan.ts` `walkNullRows` (:1145–:1230) pushes every NULL row left after the departures and the anchors into `TablePlan.unattributable`, reason `fate 4: reported, never guessed` on a fate-4 table and `no anchor names the owner` / `PARENT row X not found` / `PARENT row X has no organization` / the holder reasons on a fate-3 table; under `single` the Default Organization takes every fate-3 leftover, so a fate-3 row survives only under a wall. The plan and the inventory needed no change (A2 holds; neither is in the diff).
- The verdict moved where the defect was. `organization-ownership-apply.ts:2898` `heldUnattributable` = `table.unattributable.length` unless the inventory row is `notNullExempt`; `remainingFor` (:2906, :2908) adds it for the `attribution` and `report` fates; the post-check sums `remaining` into `discrepancies` when every step is complete (:3159), `blocking = discrepancies` (:3203), and the ledger write (`organization-ownership.ts:784–793`) passes `passed: complete && blocking === 0` to `recordDataMigrationRun`, which stamps `verified_at: null` and `blocking: N` when not passed (`migration-flag.ts:198–200`). `isDataMigrationFlagVerified` (`migration.zod.ts:278–281`) requires `verified_at` set AND `blocking === 0`; the boot guard reads it (`organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts:313`), reads `unverified`, and throws (:357). So the marker stays unverified and the v18 boot is refused, exactly as #24325 serves it. `walkNullRows` runs only for the `attribution` and `report` fates (plan.ts:1056), so the `column-drop` and `mirror-deletion` arms of `remainingFor` are rightly untouched.
- Each table, its count and the remedy: `TableOutcome.held = { rows, remedy }` (:521, :3193) with `UNATTRIBUTABLE_REMEDY` (:2887–2890); the command prints a red per-table line (`organization-ownership.ts:1031–1036`) and a summary `printError` naming every holding table with its count and the remedy (:1060–1064); `verdictCode` is 1 when `blocking` is non-zero (:1007, :1088).
- Nothing guessed, nothing deleted: no write path is touched; the pins assert the row is still present and still NULL after the blocking run (acceptance fixture `report_orphan`; walled `us_orphan` with no `DELETE` on `sys_upload_session`). ADR-0131 D10 fate 4 stands.
- A clean database still certifies, with controls: the walled control (`file_id = 'file_a'`) and both remedy re-runs read `[true, 0, 0]`; the stage-9 integration test on a booted stack keeps `[0, true, 0, unattributable]` and now also pins `held === []`. The pre-existing acceptance fixture rightly flips to `blocking: 1`, and the ablation (`heldUnattributable` forced to 0) reddens five pins including the walled one.

**(b) The `notNullExempt` exception stays advisory — A is right on the measurement; it is a reading of the ruling the seat records, not the dev's to decide.**
- Measured: `sys-sso-provider.object.ts:59` declares `tenancy: { enabled: false }`; its `organization_id` (:331–337) is "Organization scope (when org-scoped SSO is used)", better-auth's provider relation, written through the adapter with no `tenantId`; the object's own comment (:36–48) says a wall that AND-composed `organization_id = caller org` would deny every row, which is why it opts out. `engine.ts:6887` makes `tenantObject = !isTenancyDisabled(schema)` and withholds the driver scope for such an object (the :9476 docblock says the same), so the `orWhereNull` arms 8c-1 retires never run on it; `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` returns `LAYER0_NONE` on `tenancyDisabled` (`tenant-layer0-verdict.ts:137`). `git grep` on the head finds no reader among the 8c-2/8c-3 retirements (the authz resolver, `sharing-rule-service.ts`, settings, meta-write scope, bootstrap capabilities) that names `sys_sso_provider` or `sys_scim_provider`; the only non-test hits are plugin-security's private-object list and a comment. `sys_scim_provider` is retired with its table left in place untouched by the 2026-08-24 ruling, and no declaration anchors tenancy on it.
- So an organization-less row there is not "a row whose owner cannot be derived" (「找不到主人的行」, the class the maintainer chose C for): it has no owner by design, nothing 8c-1 to 8c-3 retires can darken it, and the NOT NULL exemption for both tables pre-dates the ruling (the inventory on `main`; the plan's `notNull.willReceive` reading at plan.ts:1117). B would make an operator bind a deployment-wide SSO provider to one organization (a guess that changes sign-in scope) or delete it — the harm D10 fate 4 forbids, moved onto the operator. Answer: **A**, pinned by the control (`sso_global` reported, `advisory 1`, `[true, 0, 1]`).
- The boundary: ruling 6251599171's "What it binds" reads "The verified marker then means zero NULL rows on every table (ruling β item 1)", and #24352's body quotes β item 2, "Nothing else is exempted". A reads "every table" as "every table the tenancy anchor governs" — a narrowing of the recorded letter that neither the claim nor the ruling granted. It is not blocking for this head (it changes no behaviour a tenant-scoped read sees), but it is the seat's to record, not to carry silently: the adopting seat posts reading A on #24352 inside the maintainer's veto window, as the plan does for D3, naming B as the one-line fallback (`heldUnattributable`'s `notNullExempt ? 0` arm, the control pin flips). See ③ item 8.

**(c) The advisory DEPARTURE stays advisory — right.** `advisoryDepartureReason` (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts:693–703`) answers `null` for every departure while `DECLARED_SHARING_RULE_SEEDER_RUNS` is `false` (:676, since stage 9), so on this release no departure is advisory: the declared-rule mirrors count as `remaining` and the `mirror-deletion` step performs the departure. The advisory arm is live only on a release whose boot re-seeds the rows; holding certification there would block a database on rows its own release keeps writing, with no remedy that clears. That population is a departure, not an unattributable row, so it is outside ruling C. Code path unchanged; its pins stand.

**(d) `os dev` boots only on `complete && blocking === 0` — consistent with the serving guard, and no stuck state.** The test (`dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts:173`) is exactly the ledger's `passed` and the `blocking === 0` leg of `isDataMigrationFlagVerified`; before it the loop in the docblock ("A boot refused again after a finished upgrade ends `os dev`") was reachable from a completed run with holds. The non-boot path prints each table with `remaining` above zero — held tables with `held.remedy`, any other with "the report names each" — then where the copy is and the resume command (:176–188); pinned (`sys_saved_report: 2 row(s) …`, two lines, the `--apply --plan-file … --backup-taken` command). `report.blocking !== 0` treats an absent `blocking` as holding, a safe default since the same CLI writes the report it reads.

**(e) The A5 route (a) — right, minimal, graded, and the block is clean.**
- Export: `plugin-sharing/src/index.ts:103–110` re-exports `translateDeclaredSharingRule` with `DeclaredSharingRule` and `DeclaredSharingRuleSkip` from `declared-sharing-rules.js`; the module is byte-identical to `origin/main` (the function is pure, :168–221). The three names are the function and the two components of its return type — the minimum that makes the export typeable. Graded `minor` on `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`. One definition of "served" (enforcement's own translator); the CLI's `describeDeclaredRuleSkip` (apply.ts:289–300) is a switch exhaustive over the `kind` union, so a new skip kind fails the CLI's typecheck rather than falling through — a second spelling of the reasons, not a second translator.
- Port: `judgeDeclaredSharingRules` (apply.ts:276–286) drops nameless items and judges the rest through the translator; the command's `rules()` (`organization-ownership.ts:813–825`) feeds the registry's `sharing_rule` items, else the metadata service's — the two readers enforcement uses since stage 9. `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` is already a `workspace:*` dependency of the CLI (`packages/cli/package.json:84`, pre-existing), so the dynamic import resolves in the published CLI.
- Block: `runDeclaredRuleMirrorDeletion` reads mirrors and counts grants (reads only), computes `unnameable` as mirrors with grants whose name is not served (:2653), splits undeclared from refused, and returns `blocked(blockers)` (:2680) before the first `UPDATE` (:2683 onward). Nothing is written before the block; the step is `blocked`, the ledger reads `complete: false`, and a re-run re-reads — idempotent. Each refused blocker names the rule, its rows, the translation's reason and the remedy (:2669–2679). A refused mirror no grant names is deleted like an undeclared one — stage 9's rule, unchanged. On a duplicate name `served` wins over `refused` (:2640–2644), the right precedence. Pinned both ways, and `judgeDeclaredSharingRules` is pinned over the real translator (served, untranslatable, dotted `field` recipient, match-all, nameless).
- `DeclaredSharingRulesPort.names()` → `rules()`: CLI-internal. `packages/cli` `exports` are `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body` and `./package.json`; `src/index.ts`, `src/console.ts` and `src/hook-body.ts` export nothing from `utils/organization-ownership-*`; the only implementers on the head are the command and the two test files. No FROM → TO pair is owed for it.

**(f) The operator text (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`), sentence by sentence — true against the code.**
- "A row whose owner cannot be derived blocks certification." — `heldUnattributable` → `remaining` → `discrepancies` → `blocking`. ✓
- "That covers a reported row, and a row whose anchor is missing under a wall (for example an upload session whose file is gone)." — fate 4 and the walled fate-3 leftover; inventory :475 anchors `sys_upload_session.file_id` on `sys_file`; pinned as `sys_file row file_gone not found`. ✓
- "The ceremony never guesses an owner for such a row and never deletes it." — no write path; pinned. ✓
- "The post-check names each table, its row count and the remedy: give each row its organization (write its `organization_id`, or repair the anchor its reason names), or delete it by hand, then re-run `--apply`." — `held`, `UNATTRIBUTABLE_REMEDY`, the per-table and summary lines. ✓
- "Until then the run exits `1`, the marker stays unverified, and a v18 server does not start on the database." — `verdictCode`, `recordDataMigrationRun` (`verified_at: null`, `blocking: N`), the guard's `unverified` refusal. ✓
- "A verified marker therefore means no organization-less row on any table. The one exception is a table whose `organization_id` is not the tenancy anchor (`sys_sso_provider`, and the retired `sys_scim_provider`): a row there bound to no organization is legitimate, is reported, and does not block." — matches `heldUnattributable` and the control pin. ✓ (Wording: the first sentence says "any table" and the next takes one back; see ③ N1.)
- The `os dev` paragraph (:213–215): "If a step blocks, or the post-check still holds rows (a row whose owner cannot be derived, named per table with its remedy), `os dev` stops and prints what holds it, where the copy is, and the command that resumes the run." — `holds`, `kept`, `again` in `upgradeDevelopmentDatabase`. ✓
- `install-modes.mdx` is unchanged, and its only ADR-0131 sentence is about D6 install modes (measured by the dev; not in the diff). Nothing under `content/docs/releases/` changed. ✓

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — right.** `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` names `yes (narrowing)` as the legal combination for "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; the widening is plugin-sharing's new export, the narrowings are the four below. The PR body (line 2) and the changeset (line 8 of the body) carry the same line. The claim's `no (narrowing)` was written before the A5 route was chosen; amendment 6254164222 priced route (a) as "a `Clause-②: yes` widening at `minor`", so the measured arm is the planned one.
- **FROM → TO pairs: four, complete and true, each with a one-line fix.** (1) `--apply` on a database holding an unattributable row: exit `0` / `advisory` / verified → exit `1` / `blocking` / unverified (`verdictCode`; the ledger's `passed`; `isDataMigrationFlagVerified`). (2) A database an earlier `--apply` certified while it held such a row: re-certified → unverified on the next run (the resume runs the post-check; `recordDataMigrationRun` writes `verified_at: null` and `blocking: N`). (3) `os dev` boots on `complete` → boots on `complete` and `blocking 0`. (4) The `mirror-deletion` step renamed onto any declared name → blocks while grants name a mirror of a refused rule. Nothing is missing: the port rename is internal (①(e)), `TableOutcome.held` is additive, and the `--plan` warning text is prose. The Fix lines are operator data acts plus the one code act (correct the declaration), one line each.
- **ADR-0087 marker — right disposition, right spelling.** Exactly one adr-0087 HTML-comment marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription) …why…`, the grammar `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads (header :63; `CATEGORIES` :536–543 holds the category). The category's meaning holds on the facts: no spec key, option, export or stored shape is added, removed or renamed; nothing retires, so `registered` is not owed and `runtime-export-retired`, `runtime-interface-only` and `type-surface-only` do not apply; the remedy is an operator data act `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite for. The bold **FROM** / **TO:** / **Fix:** lines are the house label convention the gate's branch 1 reads as a label, not a code-rewrite prescription (:718–723); the gate's legs (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`) are `success` on the head, and the gate reads the `(narrowing)` arm through `readClause2Line` (:683–684) so the marker was demanded and found.
- **Bumps in the launch window — right.** `@objectstack/cli: minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: minor`; no `major` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s launch-window guard); the LEVEL axis (a `yes` declaration grades at least one moved package `minor`) is met twice; `Check Changeset` is `success`. The `**BREAKING** (narrowings), shipped as minor under the launch-window convention` banner is the convention the gate states.
- Nit, not wrong: the changeset tells CHANGELOG readers about `DeclaredSharingRulesPort.rules()`, "formerly `names()`", a surface no consumer can reach.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` alias outside the claimed surface — accepted.** `scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs:380–388` lists the CLI's known unaliased test imports without `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`; the registry is shrink-only (:316); the new value imports (`organization-ownership-apply.declared-rule-mirrors.test.ts:58`, the dynamic import in apply.ts:277) therefore red the gate without an anchored alias. One anchored entry (`^@objectstack\/plugin-sharing$` → `../plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts`), spelled as its neighbours; declared in the body and the report.
2. **`yes (narrowing)` against the claim's `no (narrowing)` — answered in ②:** the measured arm, planned by amendment 6254164222 for route (a), declared identically on the body and the changeset.
3. **The changeset FROM/TO form — answered in ②:** the bold label form is the gate-readable house convention; the gate is green and every pair is present.
4. **The port rename — answered in ①(e):** CLI-internal by the `exports` map; nothing owed.
5. **The merge of `origin/main` (`db4618b5`, stage 8a) — accepted.** AGENTS.md's multi-agent discipline (§7, §9) names `git merge origin/main` as the way a branch picks up `main`; the merge was clean, the dev re-ran the suites on the merged head, and the squash landing drops the merge commit.
6. **The `wip` commit subjects — accepted.** The landing squashes (AGENTS.md ~:486), so the PR title is the subject that lands; each of the five commits carries the model-free trailer pair (`Claude-Session`, `Co-authored-by: Claude`), the one commit-message rule AGENTS.md states (~:460); the merge commit is git-generated and is discarded by the squash.
7. **The out-of-scope note — confirmed.** `18.sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired.ts:32–33` still carries the D13 paraphrase on this head; `packages/spec/src` is untouched; row 8e carries it per claim 6254514683 and amendment 6254164222.
8. **Escalation (①(b)) — the seat's act before the queue, non-blocking for this head.** Record reading A of ruling C on #24352: the marker means zero NULL rows on every table the tenancy anchor governs; `sys_sso_provider` and the retired `sys_scim_provider` (`notNullExempt`) are reported and advisory because their `organization_id` is not the tenancy anchor and no retiring NULL reader reads them. Name B as the one-line fallback. The maintainer may veto; a veto is a one-line follow-up on `heldUnattributable` and its control pin, not a reopening of this stage.

**Non-blocking wording items (prose only; a `wip` or a follow-up may carry them):**
- N1 `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:1498–1500` — fold the qualifier into the sentence: "A verified marker therefore means no organization-less row on any table the tenancy anchor governs; the one exception is …", so the paragraph does not state "any table" and then take one back.
- N2 `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts:628` — "(but on a table whose column is not the tenancy anchor)" reads as a contradiction to an operator; write "except on a table whose column is not the tenancy anchor". The same "but on" idiom is in the `heldUnattributable` docblock (apply.ts:2893–2897) and the command's comment (:1054).
- N3 `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:215` — one 120-character line in a wrapped paragraph; reflow.
